# Drag gestures freeze over an iframe pane and leave the session unterminated

## Context

Found and root-caused by @neo-opus-vega on 2026-08-30 while enhancing a private consumer workspace — the first dock consumer to embed an editor iframe as pane content. Engine apps never hit it, because no engine app puts an iframe in a dock pane. Routed to me as an engine lane per the operator's ruling that engine defects surfaced in that workspace split out from the consumer lane; the finding, the mechanism and the proof are hers.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-08-30T16:50:03Z; A2A claim sweep over the last 15 messages (all read-states) shows no competing claim — the offer message is the handoff. No equivalent found; the nearest search hit, `#12883`, is closed and unrelated. Structure-map gate: N/A, no `ai/` or Agent OS surface and no new `.mjs` file.

## The Problem

Any real pointer drag that crosses an iframe pane freezes mid-gesture. The splitter engages — `neo-drag-active` lands on `body`, `drag:start` reaches the worker — and then nothing. Once the pointer is over the iframe, `pointermove` and `pointerup` are delivered to the **iframe's** document; the parent page's sensor never sees them, so the session never ends.

The stuck `neo-drag-active` then survives the gesture and leaks into later, unrelated gestures.

**Proof of mechanism (@neo-opus-vega):** setting `pointer-events: none` on iframes and re-running the *identical* CDP drag lets the splitter commit the full 160px and clears the class. The discriminator that makes this consumer-only: engine-side `EventSimulator` gestures are element-dispatched and perform no hit-testing, so they always completed cleanly. Only real hit-tested input dies — which is exactly why no existing test sees it.

**Repro with no private code:** in `examples/dashboard/dock`, make one `resolvePane` return an iframe component (`{tag: 'iframe', src: …}`), then drag the splitter across it.

## The Architectural Reality

The pipeline already stamps the gesture on `body`:

| site | action |
|---|---|
| `src/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.mjs:160` | `document.body?.classList?.add('neo-drag-active')` |
| `src/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.mjs:215` | removed in `endGesture` |
| `src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs:424` | removed on the addon's cleanup path |

And `resources/scss/src/Global.scss:59` already consumes it:

```scss
.neo-drag-active,
.neo-drag-active * {
    user-select: none !important;
}
```

Its comment calls it a *"gesture-scoped selection guard… so a drag across card content can never become a text selection sweep"*.

**That block is the whole story.** It suppresses a native behaviour that would otherwise hijack the gesture — and `user-select` **cannot cross into a nested browsing context**. The descendant selector stops at the iframe boundary, so the guard has always had an iframe blind spot; selection was simply the less visible of the two behaviours it fails to suppress there. Pointer capture is the second, and it does not merely degrade the gesture — it ends it.

So this is not a missing feature. It is an existing, deliberately gesture-scoped guard that covers one of the two things a nested document steals.

## The Fix

1. **Extend the existing guard, in place**, so the same gesture scope suppresses iframe pointer capture:

```scss
.neo-drag-active iframe {
    pointer-events: none;
}
```

2. **Verify the scope actually covers every drag family.** `neo-drag-active` is added by the *Mouse sensor*. Whether tab drags, cross-zone drags and sort drags all route through that sensor is unverified — if any family drives a drag without it, the rule silently does not apply there. That check is part of this ticket, not an assumption in it.

3. **Terminal hygiene for a lost pointerup.** `Mouse.mjs:156` already documents that "an off-document release never reaches mouseup" and relies on the move stream observing the primary button gone. An iframe swallows the move stream too, so that fallback cannot fire either. The session needs a terminal that does not depend on input the parent document will never receive.

4. **An escape hatch** for a drag whose legitimate target *is* the iframe — an opt-out class rather than an unconditional global.

### The invariant this fix silently depends on

Raised by @neo-opus-vega, and load-bearing rather than incidental: **`pointer-events: none` also removes an element as a native drag-and-drop target**, because the same hit-testing governs `dragover` and `drop`.

That is harmless today only because `neo-drag-active` is stamped exclusively inside sensor-driven *synthetic* gestures, and a native HTML5 drag never enters the sensor. The shield is therefore scoped to sessions in which no native drop could be pending.

An engine-level native-DnD interop layer is being explored (declarative `dataTransfer` drag sources, for content that must receive real HTML5 drops — embedded editors and iframes; the workspace that surfaced this finding hand-rolled exactly that as a main addon). If it lands, an unqualified stamp would let this shield suppress the very drops that layer exists to deliver.

So the invariant is written down here rather than left implicit: **the shield class stays synthetic-session-only, and is never stamped for a native drag.** It is an acceptance criterion below, so the two features cannot collide silently later.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.neo-drag-active` | `src/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.mjs:160` | unchanged as a signal; gains a second consumer rule | none — absence restores today's freeze | the guard comment at `Global.scss:54` | CDP drag across an iframe pane completes |
| `.neo-drag-active iframe` | `resources/scss/src/Global.scss` | `pointer-events: none` for the gesture's duration | opt-out class for iframe-targeting drags | same block | before/after CDP drag, class cleared |
| `.neo-drag-passthrough` | `resources/scss/src/Global.scss` | public opt-out: an iframe carrying it stays interactive for the duration of a sensor gesture | **bounded** — it does NOT survive a DragZone session, where `draggable/DragProxyComponent.scss` applies `body:has(.neo-is-dragging) * {pointer-events: none !important}`; a universal selector with `!important` outranks any `:not()` here | stated in the rule's own comment | component arm asserting shielded-vs-opted-out against the gesture class |
| gesture terminal | `Mouse.mjs:215` / `addon/DragDrop.mjs:424` | ends a session whose pointerup was lost to another document | current move-stream fallback, which an iframe also swallows | method JSDoc | stuck-class assertion after an interrupted drag |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — this consumes an existing runtime signal and adds no new contract. Adjacent to #17836 (DockLayouts rebuild) but not gated on it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pointer drag crossing an iframe pane completes, witnessed by the gesture reaching its terminal — the sensor observing the release — rather than by splitter travel.

      **Amended 2026-08-30**, at @neo-gpt's RA-1, after both travel instruments were built and both proved wrong. Travel is unobtainable in the isolation fixture: a standalone splitter has no siblings to resize. The sensor's `drag:move` stream is worse than unobtainable — it only exists once a DragZone session is armed, and that session shields the whole page through `body:has(.neo-is-dragging) *`, so an arm that waits for the stream sits outside the window this fix covers. Measured: adding a 250ms hold to obtain it made the crossing arm pass with the fix reverted.

      Travel was only ever a proxy for "did the parent document still hold the pointer after the crossing". The release answers that directly, and it is the assertion that goes red on the defect (5.2s hang vs 0.36s green). A travel witness remains welcome in a fixture with real sibling panes; it is not what certifies this fix.
- [ ] `neo-drag-active` is cleared after that drag, and after a drag interrupted over an iframe — verified by asserting the class is absent, not by a later gesture appearing to work.
- [ ] Every drag family that stamps a gesture is enumerated, and each is shown to carry `neo-drag-active` — or the rule's scope is widened to cover the ones that do not.
- [ ] A drag whose target is legitimately the iframe still works, via the opt-out.
- [ ] Coverage uses a **hit-tested** gesture. An `EventSimulator` arm cannot fail on this defect and must not be offered as evidence.
- [ ] An assertion pins the synthetic-session-only invariant: a native HTML5 drag does not stamp the shield class, so `dragover`/`drop` targets stay hit-testable. This must fail if a future change stamps it outside a sensor-driven gesture.

## Out of Scope

- The DockLayouts rebuild (#17836).
- Cross-**window** drag (#17578) — the sibling failure at a *separate* browsing context boundary rather than a nested one. Same family, different transport; if the terminal-hygiene work generalises, that ticket benefits, but it is not resolved here.
- Any change to what `user-select` does; the selection half of the guard is correct as written.

## Avoided Traps

- **A global `iframe {pointer-events: none}`.** It would break every iframe in the product outside a drag. The value of `neo-drag-active` is that it is already gesture-scoped — the fix rides that scope rather than inventing one.
- **Proving it with `EventSimulator`.** Element-dispatched events skip hit-testing, so a simulated drag passes both before and after the fix. That is the exact shape of a green test that cannot fail on the defect, and it is why this survived to a consumer.
- **Treating the stuck class as the bug.** It is a symptom of the lost pointerup; clearing it defensively would hide an unterminated session rather than end one.

## Related

- #17836 — DockLayouts rebuild for v13.2.
- #17578 — cross-window drag never engages a target zone; the sibling document-boundary failure.
- Found by @neo-opus-vega; evidence trail available from her on request.

## AC-3 enumeration — the drag families, and where the shield class actually lands

Enumerated at `dff1e443a9`. `neo-drag-active` is added in **exactly one place**:

| site | role |
|---|---|
| `src/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.mjs:160` | **adds**, on `mousedown` — before the drag threshold |
| `src/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.mjs:215` | removes, in `endGesture` |
| `src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs:424` | removes, on the addon's cleanup path — never adds |

`src/main/draggable/sensor/Touch.mjs` is a full parallel drag path — `startDrag()` at `:212` dispatching its own `drag:start` at `:225` — and it never touches the class. `sensor/Base.mjs` is abstract (83 lines, `trigger()` only) and carries no gesture lifecycle, so there is no shared seam stamping it today.

So the honest answer to AC-3 is **no**: not every drag family carries the class. That is why the AC exists rather than being an assumption.

### Two consequences, one of which is not yet settled

**1. The stamp is deliberately early, and that constrains where it can move.** `Mouse.mjs:154` explains it brackets the *pre-threshold* window so a splitter drag cannot become a text-selection sweep. Moving the stamp to the `drag:start` listener in the addon — which would cover both sensors in one place, and where the removal already lives — would lose that pre-threshold protection. The two concerns want different timings: the selection guard needs `mousedown`, the iframe shield only needs `drag:start`.

**2. Whether Touch needs the shield at all is an open question, and I am not going to assume it.** Touch events have implicit capture: `touchmove`/`touchend` are dispatched to the `touchstart` target for the life of the touch, so a finger crossing an iframe should never hand the stream to the child document the way a mouse does. If that holds, Touch's missing class is **correct** for this fix rather than a gap, and widening the rule to touch would be scope invented from a symmetry argument.

That reasoning is spec-derived, not measured — and this harness cannot verify real hit-tested touch input. It needs a measurement on a touch device or an emulated touch stream before it becomes load-bearing. Until then the fix stays mouse-scoped, and the shield rides the existing `mousedown`-anchored class.

### Effect on the fix shape

Narrower than the original sketch: the SCSS rule lands in the existing `Global.scss:59` guard block as planned, and the "verify every drag family" work resolves to *one* sensor plus a recorded open question, rather than a refactor to a shared seam. The terminal-hygiene item is unaffected — `Mouse.mjs:156`'s documented off-document-release fallback relies on the move stream, which an iframe swallows too.

* fix(draggable): shield iframes for the duration of a synthetic drag (#17883)

A pointer drag crossing an iframe pane froze mid-gesture. Once the cursor is over an
iframe, mousemove and mouseup are delivered to the CHILD document, so the parent's sensor
never observes the release: the splitter stops short and the gesture class outlives the
drag, leaking into later gestures elsewhere.

The fix extends the guard that already exists for the same reason rather than adding a new
mechanism. `.neo-drag-active` is a gesture-scoped selection guard — `user-select: none`, so
a drag across card content cannot become a text-selection sweep — and `user-select` stops
dead at the iframe boundary. That guard has always had this blind spot; selection was simply
the less visible of the two native behaviours a nested browsing context steals. Pointer
capture is the second, and it does not degrade the gesture, it ends it.

stamped only inside sensor-driven synthetic gestures and never for a native drag, so the
shield cannot suppress a real HTML5 drop. An iframe that is legitimately drag-targetable
opts out with `neo-drag-passthrough`.

Coverage is hit-tested via `page.mouse`, deliberately. Events dispatched onto an element
perform no hit-testing, so an EventSimulator drag completes identically with and without the
fix — structurally incapable of failing here, which is why this reached a consumer with the
suite green.

the iframe entirely and it passed with the fix reverted, asserting only that a stylesheet

never reached the sensor". Components suite 104 passed.

makes the gesture scope an invariant rather than a detail.
